source.name: Chuck's Guide to the AH-64D Apache Block II
source.version_or_date: Last Updated: 7/09/2024 (as printed in the PDF header) - guide has since grown to 927 pages per the copy used, so this may be a newer edition; re-check chucksguides.com periodically

_extraction_note: Steps below were extracted directly from the guide's own numbered [P]/[CPG] checklist format, not generated. Some sub-steps were dropped where the PDF's multi-column kneeboard layout split a sentence across a graphic sidebar and the extraction tool couldn't reliably rejoin it (step numbers may skip, e.g. 6 to 9) - these are minor sub-bullets/notes, not missing major actions, but you or Marky should do one real read-through against the PDF before treating this as complete. No standalone 'aircraft shutdown' checklist exists in this guide (verified by full-text search) - it covers Cold Start in extreme depth but not a formal post-flight shutdown sequence. Weapons audit (explicit request: check for missing weapons instructions, starting with the A-10C and then this aircraft). Part 14 of the guide (Offence: Weapons & Armament) was compared section by section against this file. The weapon TYPES were already all present (gun, rockets, AGM-114K, AGM-114L); what was missing were whole delivery methods. Added: gun FIXED mode (2.2.2), CPG gun NORM with HMD (2.3.1) and with TADS (2.3.2), gun with George AI (2.4); rocket running/diving fire (3.2.2), multicrew direct fire (3.3.1) and indirect fire (3.3.2) in COOP mode with the TADS, rockets with George AI (3.4); plus the first systems_notes in this file (9 reference notes condensed/written independently from sections 1.1-1.6, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1: armament overview, Hydra rocket types, crew roles, WAS/trigger guard, delivery techniques, gun ranging/limits, rocket aiming, Hellfire constraints box, Hellfire missile settings/channels/laser codes). Every procedure is condensed/paraphrased from the guide's own numbered [P]/[CPG] steps. Also fixed a stale sentence in the LOBL entry that said the LOAL modes were 'not yet transcribed' (they already were). NOT yet carried over, stated rather than left as a silent gap: section 4.2.1.4 (operating with a JTAC/AFAC - contact and 9-line procedure, coordinates + IR pointer, laser designation) and 4.2.2 (Hellfire with George AI as CPG) - both read but not transcribed; the guide's worked JTAC examples use specific frequencies/callsigns from its own demo mission, which should be generalized rather than baked in. The step-number gaps noted at the top of this note still apply to the older entries.

before_start_up.action: [P+CPG] If required during night operations, turn on flashlight (LALT+L).
[P+CPG] To view the cockpit more easily, remove the IHADSS monocle by pressing "I".
[P] Insert Ignition Key and set MSTR IGN (Master Ignition) Selector to BATT (Battery).
[P+CPG] Set Signal Lights Control Knob to BRT (Bright).
[P+CPG] Set NVS (Night Vision System) Mode Switch to OFF (AFT).
[P+CPG] Set KU (Keyboard Unit) Brightness Knob to Bright (turn clockwise as required).
[P+CPG] Set MPD Mode Selector to DAY for day operations, or NT for night operations.
[P+CPG] Set EUFD Brightness Control Knob to Bright (turn clockwise as required).
[CPG] Set TDU (TEDAC Display Unit) Mode Selector to DAY or NT as appropriate.
[P+CPG] Adjust VHF, UHF, FM1, FM2 and HF Radio Volume as required.
[P+CPG] Adjust SENS (Sensitivity) Control Knob as required.
[P+CPG] Set ICS (Intercom System) Switch to VOX (middle).
[P+CPG] Adjust IFF, RLWR, and ADF as required.
[P+CPG] Close Cockpit Door (LCTRL+C or click the door handle).

apu_start.action: [P] Flip the APU Start Button Guard.
[P] Press the APU Start Button for 1-2 seconds, then release.
[P] During APU start-up, watch for advisories on the EUFD (APU START active).
[P] When APU start-up completes: 'ON' light illuminates on APU Start Button; EUFD shows APU POWER ON, and APU START / ACCUM OIL PRES LO advisories clear.
[P] Once started, the APU generator powers the MPDs and other helicopter systems.
[P] During extended APU operation, monitor XMSN OIL temperature on the ENG SYS page.

systems_setup_dms_sweep.action: [P/CPG] Press VAB next to MASTER LOAD to load the DTU (Data Transfer Unit).
[P/CPG] Turn on radar altimeter (press VAB next to RDR ALT).
[P/CPG] Press VAB next to SET again to exit the FLT SET sub-menu.
[P/CPG] Press VAB next to Chaff Arm/Safe to toggle SAFE to ARM (must be airborne, weight-on-wheels interlock).
[P/CPG] Turn on Doppler Navigation System (press VAB next to DOPPLER).
[P/CPG] While nav alignment runs, wait until position confidence stabilizes.
[P/CPG] Nav system alignment typically takes ~4-5 minutes.
[CPG] Press VAB next to LASER to power the LRFD (Laser Rangefinder/Designator).
[CPG] Press VAB next to UTIL to return to the main WPN page.
[P/CPG] Press the FCR FAB to access the Fire Control Radar page.
[P/CPG] Press VAB next to UTIL to select the Utility page.
[P/CPG] FCR NOT POWERED indication should be visible until powered.
[P/CPG] Note the AN/APR-48 RFI may still be powered independently for threat warning.

ihadss_boresight.action: [P+CPG] Press the WPN FAB to access the Weapon menu.
[P+CPG] Press VAB next to IHADSS to activate the Boresight Reticle Unit (BRU).
[P+CPG] Position your head naturally and aim the HDU line-of-sight reticle at the boresight target.
[P+CPG] If accepted, the BRU bullseye extinguishes and B/S NOW clears from the IHADSS menu.
[P+CPG] Adjust HDU Symbology Brightness as required.

engine_start.action: [P] Set RTR BRK (Rotor Brake) Switch to FWD (OFF).
[P] Check both Power Levers are set to OFF (fully aft).
[P] Select the ENG page (press the A/C FAB).
[P] Confirm initiation of the left (No. 1) engine start sequence.
[P] Move left Power Lever to IDLE (RALT+HOME). Fuel flow and ignition begin.
[P] Wait for left engine parameters to stabilize (see guide for exact NG/NP/torque figures).
[P] Set Right (No. 2) Engine Start Switch to START (fwd) for 1-2 seconds, then release.
[P] Move right Power Lever to IDLE (RSHIFT+HOME). Fuel flow and ignition begin.
[P] Wait for right engine parameters to stabilize.
[P] If required, reset MSTR WARN and MSTR CAUT pushbuttons.
[P] Monitor the ENG page for abnormal engine parameters.
[P] Monitor the ENG SYS sub-page for abnormal engine parameters.
[P] Before advancing power levers to FLY, confirm both ENG 1 and ENG 2 OIL PSI are in range.
[P] Slowly advance both Power Levers to FLY.
[P] Confirm LOW ROTOR RPM advisory is not shown on the EUFD.
[P] Press the APU Start Button for 1-2 seconds to shut down the APU (no longer needed once engines are running).

after_start_up.action: [P] Uncage the SAI (Standby Attitude Indicator) by pulling and turning the caging knob; confirm the red OFF flag disappears.
[P] Set CMWS Power/Test Knob to ON.
[P] Set CMWS Display Brightness Control Knob as required.

defensive_systems_cmws_setup.action: [P] Set CMWS (Common Missile Warning System) Power/Test Knob to ON.
[P] Set CMWS Display Brightness Control Knob as required.
[P] Set CMWS Bypass/Auto Switch as desired - Chuck's Guide recommends BYPASS since AUTO can waste flares needlessly.
[P] Adjust Missile Warning System volume via the ADF Auxiliary System Volume Knob (note: this disables ADF navaid audio while active).
[P] Set the CMWS Arm/Safe Switch to ARM (up).
[P] Consult the CMWS Indicator Display for missile launch direction/audio warnings.

defensive_systems_chaff_manual.action: [P/CPG] From the ASE page, press VAB next to 'CHAFF' to arm chaff.
[P/CPG] Press VAB next to 'CHAFF MODE' and set release mode to MANUAL.
[P/CPG] Press the Chaff Dispense Button on the cyclic to dispense a single chaff.
[P/CPG] Chaff counters are visible on the ASE page, WPN page, and the CMWS panel (pilot only).

defensive_systems_chaff_programmed.action: [P/CPG] From the ASE page, press VAB next to 'CHAFF' to arm chaff.
[P/CPG] Press VAB next to 'CHAFF MODE' and set release mode to PROGRAM.
[P/CPG] Press VAB next to 'UTIL' to enter the ASE Utility sub-page.
[P/CPG] Set Burst Counter, Burst Interval, Salvo Count, and Salvo Interval via the associated VABs.
[P/CPG] Press the Chaff Dispense Button on the cyclic to dispense chaff as programmed.
[P/CPG] Chaff counters are visible on the ASE page, WPN page, and the CMWS panel (pilot only).

defensive_systems_flares_bypass_mode.action: [P] Set CMWS Power/Test Knob to ON.
[P] Set CMWS Display Brightness Control Knob as required.
[P] Set CMWS Bypass/Auto Switch to BYPASS.
[P] Set the CMWS Arm/Safe Switch to ARM (up).
[P] Press the Flare Dispense Button to dispense the flare program manually. Note: in BYPASS mode, flares are never dispensed automatically - you control every release.

defensive_systems_flares_auto_mode.action: [P] Set CMWS Power/Test Knob to ON.
[P] Set CMWS Display Brightness Control Knob as required.
[P] Set CMWS Bypass/Auto Switch to AUTO.
[P] Set the CMWS Arm/Safe Switch to ARM (up).
[P] In AUTO mode, flares dispense automatically per the preset flare program (set on the ground, engines off, or via Mission Editor).
[P] You can still press the Flare Dispense Button to manually trigger the flare program if desired.

defensive_systems_flare_jettison.action: [P] Set CMWS Power/Test Knob to ON.
[P] Set the CMWS Arm/Safe Switch to ARM (up).
[P] Flip the Flare Jettison Cover up, then switch JETTISON up to jettison flares. Used in a forced-landing situation since flares are a fire hazard.

weapons.name: M230 30mm Chain Gun
weapons.employment_notes: Standard gun employment steps per Chuck's Guide section 2.2, NORM mode with HMD (pilot). Other gun entries below: FIXED mode (pilot), NORM with HMD (CPG), NORM with TADS (CPG) and George AI as CPG.
switchology: [P] Set Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD). HDU should show 'P-HMD'.

switchology.text: [P] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [P] Press WAS (Weapon Action Switch) UP to select the Gun.
[P] Flip Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN).
[P] Press VAB next to MAN RNG to set gun ranging distance.
[P] Press VAB next to desired BURST LIMIT setting.
[P] Fire by squeezing the Weapons Trigger, second detent (default Spacebar binding).

weapons.name: M230 30mm Chain Gun - FIXED Mode (Pilot)
weapons.employment_notes: Chuck's Guide section 2.2.2. Point-the-nose gunnery: in FIXED mode the turret stays pointed straight ahead at a set ballistic solution of 1575 m instead of following your helmet sight, and the Fixed Gun Reticle marks where that solution lands - you aim by maneuvering the helicopter. For the head-tracked NORM mode see the main M230 entry.
switchology: [P] Set the Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD). The HDU should show 'P-HMD'.

switchology.text: [P] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [P] Press WAS (Weapon Action Switch) UP to select the Gun. The range source reverts to manual, which doesn't affect the gun's range compensation in FIXED mode.
[P] Flip the Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN) (not needed if the Weapons Trigger Guard Enable special option is turned off).
[P] Press the WPN FAB (Fixed Action Button) to open the Weapon menu.
[P] Press the VAB (Variable Action Button) next to the desired BURST LIMIT (the guide's example uses 20 rounds).
[P] Press the VAB next to MODE to select FXD (Fixed).
[P] Note the Fixed Gun Reticle - it is the virtual point in front of the aircraft that matches the 1575 m ballistic solution.
[P] Maneuver the helicopter to place the Fixed Gun Reticle on the target.
[P] Fire by squeezing the Weapons Trigger to the second detent (default Spacebar binding).
[P] Watch where the rounds land and adjust your aim for follow-up attacks.

weapons.name: M230 30mm Chain Gun - NORM Mode with HMD (CPG)
weapons.employment_notes: Chuck's Guide section 2.3.1. The front-seat version of the pilot's head-tracked gun procedure: same steps, but using the TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS and trigger, and the HDU shows 'C-HMD'. The turret follows your helmet line-of-sight reticle and compensates for range. Reference: section 2.1 for ranging, turret limits and limit messages (see the gun reference note).
switchology: [CPG] Set the Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD). The HDU should show 'C-HMD'.

switchology.text: [CPG] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [CPG] Press the TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS (Weapon Action Switch) UP to select the Gun. The range source reverts to the manual range set on the WPN page.
[CPG] Flip the TEDAC Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN) (not needed if the Weapons Trigger Guard Enable special option is turned off).
[CPG] Press the WPN FAB (Fixed Action Button) to open the Weapon menu.

[CPG] Press the VAB next to MAN RNG, enter the gun ranging distance in meters on the KU and press ENTER - 800 m is a good fixed setting. For automatic ranging enter 'A' instead (the radar altimeter must be on).
[CPG] Press the VAB next to the desired BURST LIMIT (the guide's example uses 10 rounds).
[CPG] Press the VAB next to MODE to select NORM.
[CPG] Verify no COINCIDENCE, AZ LIMIT, EL LIMIT or BAL LIMIT messages appear in the High Action Display.

[CPG] Move your head to keep the Helmet Line-of-Sight Reticle on the target - the turret follows the reticle and compensates for range. Maximum supported ballistic range is 4200 m; the guide's author prefers 500-1800 m.
[CPG] Fire by squeezing the TEDAC Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger to the second detent.

weapons.name: M230 30mm Chain Gun - NORM Mode with TADS (CPG)
weapons.employment_notes: Chuck's Guide section 2.3.2. Guns the target using the TADS as the sight, with the laser rangefinder feeding range and (with LMC + TSE) automatic lead on moving targets. Multicrew note: on the pilot's HDU the Cued Line-of-Sight Reticle shows where the TADS is looking when the pilot's ACQ source is TADS. Target of opportunity spotted by eye? Select the GHS (your helmet) or PHS (pilot's helmet) as the acquisition source and press the Sight Slave Button to slave the TADS to the helmet reticle; press it again to de-slave and fine-tune with MAN TRK.
switchology: [CPG] From the WPN page, press the VAB next to UTIL to open the Weapon Utility page.
[CPG] Press the VABs next to TADS and FLIR to power them on if needed (hollow circle = OFF, solid circle = ON).
[CPG] Press the VAB next to LASER to power on the laser rangefinder/designator (LRFD) - only the CPG can do this.
[CPG] Press the VAB next to UTIL to return to the main WPN page.

[CPG] Set the Sight Select Switch to RIGHT (TADS). 'TADS' appears at the lower left of the TDU and HDU. To clear the TADS overlay from the HDU either flip the HDU away with the IHADSS Show binding (default 'i'), or set the sight to FWD (HMD), turn the TDU Image Brightness rocker fully DOWN, then set the sight back to TADS.

switchology.text: [CPG] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [CPG] Press the TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS UP to select the Gun.
[CPG] Flip the TEDAC Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN) (not needed if the Weapons Trigger Guard Enable special option is turned off).
[CPG] Press the WPN FAB, then the VAB next to the desired BURST LIMIT (the guide's example uses 10 rounds), then the VAB next to MODE to select NORM.
[CPG] Confirm TADS is the selected sight on the WPN page, select the TADS video with the TAD button, and adjust the TDU symbology (SYM), image brightness (BRT) and contrast (CON) as needed.

[CPG] On the TEDAC Left Hand Grip set the TADS Sensor Select Switch to FLIR (FWD) for infrared or DTV (MIDDLE) for day TV. If FLIR: adjust Level and Gain, and toggle polarity with the TEDAC Right Hand Grip FLIR Polarity Button or the collective Boresight/Polarity Selector RIGHT (PLRT).
[CPG] On the TEDAC Left Hand Grip set the TADS FOV selector as desired (Zoom, Medium, Narrow or Wide).

[CPG] Slew the TADS line of sight with the TEDAC Right Hand Grip MAN TRK switch (the 'thumb force controller'). The TADS is not ground-stabilized while you use it, so keep the reticle on the target with constant small corrections.

[CPG] If the target or the helicopter is moving, press the TEDAC Left Hand Grip LMC button to engage the Linear Motion Compensator - it makes the reticle much easier to hold and also enables the Target State Estimator (TSE).

[CPG] Squeeze and hold the TEDAC Right Hand Grip LRFD Trigger: first detent = range only, second detent = range and laser designation. With LMC active, the second detent also engages TSE, which automatically leads the target so the rounds land where it's going.
[CPG] Stay inside the gun's ballistic range (4200 m maximum; the guide's author prefers 500-1800 m), then fire by squeezing the TEDAC Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger to the second detent.
[CPG] Once the target is destroyed, press the LMC button again to disengage LMC.

weapons.name: M230 30mm Chain Gun (George AI as CPG)
weapons.employment_notes: Chuck's Guide section 2.4 - the single-player way to use the gun's TADS-quality targeting: you fly and give orders, George (the AI co-pilot/gunner) finds, lases, stores and fires on the target. The George menu color shows your rules of engagement: yellow = weapons hold, green = weapons free.
switchology: [P] Set the Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD). The HDU should show 'P-HMD'.

switchology.text: [P] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [P] Show the George menu with LCTRL+V.
[P] Press 'A' SHORT (LEFT, under 0.5 sec) to cycle weapons until GUN is selected.
[P] Press 'D' SHORT (RIGHT, under 0.5 sec) to cycle the gun burst setting (the guide's example uses 20 rounds).
[P] Confirm the George menu is yellow (weapons hold). If it's green (weapons free), press 'W' LONG (UP, over 0.5 sec) to set it back to weapons hold.

[P] From the WPN page set the Pilot Acquisition Source to TADS, then fly toward the target and keep the helicopter's attitude stable. Your HDU reticle is the Designation Reticle that shows George where to look for targets.
[P] Move your head so the reticle is near the area George should search, then press 'W' SHORT (under 0.5 sec).

[George] George sets the acquisition source to PHS (Pilot Helmet Sight), slaves the TADS ('slaving'), then de-slaves it ('de-slaved') once the TADS is roughly on the area you pointed at - you can look elsewhere from here.
[George] George scans the area and, when targets are found, a target list appears in the George menu.
[P] Cycle the list with 'W' SHORT (UP) or 'S' SHORT (DOWN) until the target you want is marked with '>', then press 'D' SHORT (RIGHT) to select it. Pressing 'S' SHORT undesignates George's target.
[George] George designates, lases and stores the target with the TADS, calling out 'lased and stored'. With your ACQ source on TADS you'll see a cued line-of-sight reticle on your HDU marking it.
[P] Order George to fire with the George AI Multifunctional Input (Center) command (formerly 'Consent to Fire'), or press 'W' LONG to go weapons free (the menu turns green).
[George] George fires on the target using the burst setting you selected.
[P] To stop George engaging, press 'S' SHORT (DOWN) to undesignate his target. Hide the George menu with LCTRL+V.

weapons.name: 2.75in Rockets
weapons.employment_notes: Standard rocket employment steps per Chuck's Guide, lateral (roll) or pedal-turn steering onto the Rocket Steering Cursor depending on cockpit/mode. More detailed rocket entries follow: running/diving fire (pilot), direct and indirect COOP fire with the TADS (multicrew) and George AI as CPG.
switchology: [P] Set Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD).

switchology.text: [P] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [P] Press WAS (Weapon Action Switch) LEFT to select Rockets.
[P] Flip Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN).
[P] Press VAB next to desired rocket type.
[P] Press VAB next to MAN RNG to set ranging distance.
[P] Press VAB next to desired Salvo Quantity.
[P] Steer the Rocket Steering Cursor onto the target using pedals or cyclic roll depending on configuration.
[P] Fire by squeezing the Weapons Trigger, second detent (default Spacebar binding).

weapons.name: 2.75in Rockets - Running/Diving Fire with HMD (Pilot)
weapons.employment_notes: Chuck's Guide section 3.2.2. Same setup as the hover-fire rocket procedure, but flown as a running or diving attack: you steer onto the Rocket Steering Cursor with cyclic roll (not pedals), keep the trim ball centered with the pedals, and set pitch with the cyclic if you're diving. The articulated pylons handle rocket elevation (never azimuth) so the salvo lands on the aimpoint.
switchology: [P] Set the Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD). The HDU should show 'P-HMD'.

switchology.text: [P] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [P] Press WAS (Weapon Action Switch) LEFT to select the Rockets. A 'TYPE?' indication means no rocket type has been chosen yet.
[P] Flip the Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN) (not needed if the Weapons Trigger Guard Enable special option is turned off).
[P] Press the WPN FAB (Fixed Action Button) to open the Weapon menu.
[P] Press the VAB next to the rocket type you want (the guide's example is 6PD - high explosive, point-detonation fuzing). The rocket counter sits below the type field.
[P] Press the VAB next to MAN RNG and enter the ranging distance in meters on the KU, then ENTER - or enter 'A' for automatic ranging (radar altimeter must be on).
[P] Press the VAB next to the desired Salvo Quantity (the guide's example uses 4 rockets per salvo).
[P] Spot the target visually and start flying toward it, moving your head to keep the Helmet Line-of-Sight Reticle on it.
[P] Use cyclic roll to turn toward the Rocket Steering Cursor while keeping the reticle on the target.

[P] When the Rocket Steering Cursor lines up with the reticle laterally, stop turning and stabilize attitude and heading with the cyclic. Keep the trim ball centered with the pedals. If you're diving, set the pitch with the cyclic and hold your power setting with the collective.
[P] Verify no weapon inhibit messages (e.g. PYLON LIMITS) appear in the High Action Display.
[P] Fire by squeezing the Weapons Trigger to the second detent (default Spacebar binding).

weapons.name: 2.75in Rockets - Direct Fire, COOP Mode with TADS (Multicrew)
weapons.employment_notes: Chuck's Guide section 3.3.1. COOP mode means both crew have selected rockets and work together: the CPG designates the target with the TADS, the pilot steers onto the Rocket Steering Cursor and fires. 'Direct' means there's a clear line of sight between the TADS and the target. The CPG cues the pilot with the call 'Match and Shoot'. The COOP indication appears on the WPN page once both crew have selected rockets.
switchology: [P] Set the Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD). The HDU should show 'P-HMD'.

switchology.text: [P] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [P] Press WAS LEFT to select the Rockets ('TYPE?' means no rocket type chosen yet).
[P] Flip the Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN) (not needed if the Weapons Trigger Guard Enable special option is turned off).

[P] Press the WPN FAB, then the VAB next to the rocket type you want (example: 6PD), the VAB next to MAN RNG (enter meters on the KU, or 'A' for automatic ranging), and the VAB next to the Salvo Quantity (example: 4).
[P] Press the VAB next to ACQ and select TADS, so the CPG's TADS is your acquisition source.
[CPG] From the WPN page, press the VAB next to UTIL, power on TADS and FLIR if needed, power on LASER, then press UTIL again to return to the main WPN page.
[CPG] Set the Sight Select Switch to RIGHT (TADS). ('TADS' appears at the lower left of the TDU and HDU.)
[CPG] Press the TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS LEFT to select the Rockets, then press the WPN FAB and set the same rocket type and MAN RNG ranging as above.
[CPG] When both crew have rockets selected, COOP shows on the WPN pages. Confirm TADS is the selected sight, select the TADS video with the TAD button, and adjust SYM/BRT/CON as needed.
[CPG] Set the TADS Sensor Select Switch (TEDAC Left Hand Grip) to FLIR or DTV, adjust FLIR Level/Gain and polarity if using FLIR, and set the FOV selector as desired.

[CPG] Slew the TADS onto the target with the TEDAC Right Hand Grip MAN TRK switch (it is not ground-stabilized while you use it). If the target or aircraft is moving, press the LMC button to engage the Linear Motion Compensator (this also enables TSE).
[CPG] Squeeze and hold the TEDAC Right Hand Grip LRFD Trigger to the second detent to range and designate the target (with LMC active this also engages TSE, which leads a moving target).
[CPG] Tell the pilot 'Match and Shoot'.

[P] Steer toward the Rocket Steering Cursor until it lines up with the aimpoint - pedals in a hover, or cyclic roll in forward flight with the trim ball centered. A cued line-of-sight reticle on your HDU shows where the TADS is looking when your ACQ source is TADS.
[P] The articulated pylons set rocket elevation (not azimuth). Verify no PYLON LIMITS or other inhibit messages, then fire by squeezing the Weapons Trigger to the second detent.

[CPG] After the salvo, a TOF (time-of-flight) count runs until impact. 'Sense' the strike: drop the TADS FOV one level with the TEDAC Left Hand Grip FOV selector to watch the impacts, adjust the aimpoint, and repeat with the pilot until the desired effect.

weapons.name: 2.75in Rockets - Indirect Fire, COOP Mode with TADS (Multicrew)
weapons.employment_notes: Chuck's Guide section 3.3.2. Rocket artillery: no line of sight between the TADS and the target is needed - the CPG stores the target as a target point, slaves the TADS to that point, and the pilot 'matches and shoots' on the Rocket Steering Cursor. Can be flown from a hover or as a diving attack. Flow: CPG finds, lases, designates and stores the target; CPG selects the stored target point; both crew select rockets; pilot matches and shoots.
switchology: [P] Set the Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD), Master Arm ON (A/S pushbutton), WAS LEFT to select Rockets, then flip the Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP - same as the direct-fire procedure.

[P] Press the WPN FAB, then set the rocket type (example: 6PD), MAN RNG (meters on the KU, or 'A' for automatic ranging) and Salvo Quantity (example: 4) via their VABs, and press the VAB next to ACQ to select TADS.
[CPG] From the WPN page, press the VAB next to UTIL, power on TADS, FLIR and LASER, then press UTIL again to return. Set the Sight Select Switch to RIGHT (TADS).
[CPG] Press the TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS LEFT to select the Rockets and set the same rocket type and ranging on the WPN page. When both crew have rockets selected, COOP appears on the WPN pages.

[CPG] Confirm TADS is the selected sight, select the TADS video with the TAD button, set FLIR or DTV, adjust brightness/contrast and FOV, and slew onto the target with the MAN TRK switch (engage LMC if anything is moving).
[CPG] Squeeze and hold the TEDAC Right Hand Grip LRFD Trigger to the second detent to range and designate the target.

[CPG] Press the TEDAC Left Hand Grip Store/Update Switch FWD (STORE) to store the TADS line of sight as a target point. A 'T' and its target point number (e.g. T01) shows on the TDU - call it out to the pilot, e.g. 'BMP stored target 01'.
[CPG] On the TSD page select the ATK (Attack) phase, press the VAB next to COORD, then the VAB next to the target point (e.g. T01) - it becomes the acquisition source.
[CPG] Press the TEDAC Right Hand Grip Sight Slave Button - the TADS locks onto the selected acquisition source (the target point).
[CPG] Tell the pilot 'Match and Shoot'.

[P] Steer toward the Rocket Steering Cursor until it lines up with the aimpoint - pedals in a hover, or cyclic roll in forward flight with the trim ball centered. The cued line-of-sight reticle on your HDU marks the TADS aimpoint when your ACQ source is TADS.
[P] Verify no weapon inhibit messages (e.g. PYLON LIMITS), then fire by squeezing the Weapons Trigger to the second detent.
[CPG] 'Sense' the impacts - drop the TADS FOV one level, adjust the aimpoint, and repeat the salvo with the pilot as needed.

weapons.name: 2.75in Rockets (George AI as CPG)
weapons.employment_notes: Chuck's Guide section 3.4. Single-player rocket attack with George (the AI co-pilot/gunner) designating: you point him at an area, pick a target from his list, then match the aircraft to the Rocket Steering Cursor and give the fire order. The George menu color shows your rules of engagement: yellow = weapons hold, green = weapons free.
switchology: [P] Set the Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD). The HDU should show 'P-HMD'.

switchology.text: [P] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [P] Show the George menu with LCTRL+V.
[P] Press 'A' SHORT (LEFT, under 0.5 sec) to cycle weapons until Rockets is selected.
[P] Press 'A' LONG (LEFT, over 0.5 sec) to cycle rocket types (the guide's example selects HE).
[P] Press 'D' SHORT (RIGHT, under 0.5 sec) to cycle the salvo quantity (the guide's example uses 4 rockets per salvo).
[P] Confirm the George menu is yellow (weapons hold). If it's green (weapons free), press 'W' LONG (UP, over 0.5 sec) to set it back to weapons hold.

[P] Your HDU reticle is the Designation Reticle showing George where to look for targets. From the WPN page set the Pilot Acquisition Source to TADS, fly toward the target and keep the helicopter stable.
[P] Move your head so the reticle is near the area George should search, then press 'W' SHORT (under 0.5 sec).

[George] George sets the acquisition source to PHS (Pilot Helmet Sight), slaves the TADS ('slaving'), then de-slaves it ('de-slaved') when it's roughly on that area, and starts scanning - a target list appears when targets are found.
[P] Cycle the list with 'W' SHORT (UP) or 'S' SHORT (DOWN) until the target you want is marked '>', then press 'D' SHORT (RIGHT) to select it ('S' SHORT undesignates).
[George] George designates, lases and stores the target with the TADS ('lased and stored'). With your ACQ source on TADS, a cued line-of-sight reticle marks it on your HDU.
[P] Steer toward the Rocket Steering Cursor to 'match' (align) the helicopter with the target - pedals in a hover, cyclic roll in forward flight.
[P] Order George to fire with the George AI Multifunctional Input (Center) command (formerly 'Consent to Fire'), or press 'W' LONG to go weapons free (menu turns green).
[George] George fires the rockets at the target himself.
[P] To stop George engaging, press 'S' SHORT (DOWN) to undesignate his target. Hide the George menu with LCTRL+V.

weapons.name: AGM-114K Hellfire (Laser-Guided, LOBL)
weapons.employment_notes: Lock-On Before Launch engagement per Chuck's Guide section 4.2.1.1: the CPG lases the target with the TADS LRFD, then fires - missile tracks the laser to impact. This is the primary/most common Hellfire engagement method covered in the guide. The two other modes (LOAL-DIR and LOAL-LO / LOAL-HI) have their own entries below, for cases like backscatter or minimizing exposure time.
switchology: [CPG] From the WPN page, press VAB next to UTIL to select the Weapon Utility page.
[CPG] Press VABs next to TADS and FLIR to power those systems on if needed.
[CPG] Press VAB next to LASER to power on the LRFD (only the CPG can do this).
[CPG] Press VAB next to UTIL to return to the main WPN page.

switchology.text: [CPG] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [CPG] Press TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS RIGHT to select Missiles.
[CPG] Flip TEDAC Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN).
[CPG] Set Missile Type to SAL (Semi-Active Laser).
[CPG] Set Missile Mode to NORMAL.
[CPG] Set Missile Trajectory to DIR (Direct).
[CPG] Set LRFD Mode Selector as required (commonly LAST).
[CPG] Set Missile Priority/Alternate laser codes via the CHAN sub-page as briefed.
[CPG] Set the Sight Select Switch to RIGHT (TADS).
[CPG] Slew the TADS Line-of-Sight onto the target using the Right Hand Grip.
[CPG] Squeeze and hold the Right Hand Grip LRFD Trigger to lase and designate the target.
[CPG] Verify no weapon inhibit messages (e.g. SKR LIMIT, YAW LIMIT) and that PRI CHAN TRK is displayed.
[CPG] While continuing to lase, fire the missile by squeezing the Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger, second detent.
[CPG] Keep lasing the target continuously until missile impact - the missile tracks the laser to the target.

weapons.name: AGM-114K Hellfire (Laser-Guided, LOAL-DIR)
weapons.employment_notes: Lock-On After Launch, Direct trajectory, per Chuck's Guide section 4.2.1.2. CPG fires first, then lases - missile seeker is slaved to the TADS/HMD line-of-sight. Used to minimize exposure time or when backscatter (dust/smoke/fire between aircraft and target) prevents a clean LOBL lock. If the TADS line-of-sight and missile seeker differ by more than 2 degrees at launch, a BACKSCATTER message blocks the launch.
switchology: [CPG] Complete the same power-up/arming steps as LOBL, but set Missile Trajectory to DIR (Direct).
[CPG] Fire the missile first (direct trajectory).
[CPG] Lase the target with the TADS LRFD.
[CPG] Missile tracks the laser until impact - keep lasing continuously.

weapons.name: AGM-114K Hellfire (Laser-Guided, LOAL-LO / LOAL-HI)
weapons.employment_notes: Lock-On After Launch, Low or High trajectory, per Chuck's Guide section 4.2.1.3. CPG fires first; missile climbs shallow (LO) or steep (HI) to clear an obstacle, allowing a stand-off shot from behind cover before popping up to lase for terminal guidance. In LO/HI mode the missile seeker is caged to the most recently selected TSD target point, not the active sight.
switchology: [CPG] Select the target point as your ACQ (Acquisition Source) on the TSD before firing.
[CPG] Fire the missile (low trajectory for LOAL-LO, high trajectory for LOAL-HI).
[CPG] Pop up from cover and lase the target with the TADS.
[CPG] Missile tracks the laser until impact - keep lasing continuously.

weapons.name: AGM-114L Hellfire (Radar-Guided, without FCR)
weapons.employment_notes: Fire-and-forget radar-guided missile, TADS-designated targeting per Chuck's Guide section 4.3.1.1. Unlike the AGM-114K, this variant does not track a laser - once fired it homes on the target autonomously, so continuous lasing after launch is not required.
switchology: [CPG] From the WPN page, press VAB next to UTIL, then power on TADS/FLIR/LASER as needed, then VAB next to UTIL to return.
[CPG] Set the Sight Select Switch to RIGHT (TADS).

switchology.text: [CPG] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [CPG] Press TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS RIGHT to select Missiles.
[CPG] Flip TEDAC Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN).
[CPG] Confirm the selected sight is the TADS via the WPN page and select TADS video feed (TAD button).
[CPG] Slew the TADS Line-of-Sight onto the target.
[CPG] Squeeze and hold the Right Hand Grip LRFD Trigger to designate the target (this provides target data to the missile, not laser tracking).
[CPG] Verify no weapon inhibit messages (e.g. SKR LIMIT, YAW LIMIT) are displayed.
[CPG] Fire by squeezing the Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger, second detent.
[CPG] Missile is fire-and-forget - it homes on the target autonomously after launch.

weapons.name: AGM-114L Hellfire (Radar-Guided, with FCR)
weapons.employment_notes: Fire-and-forget radar-guided missile, FCR (Fire Control Radar) designated targeting per Chuck's Guide section 4.3.1.2. The FCR automatically locates and ranges the Next-to-Shoot (NTS) target - this is the primary use case for the AGM-114L, letting the radar do target detection instead of the TADS.
switchology: [CPG] From the WPN page, press VAB next to UTIL, power on TADS/FLIR/FCR as needed, then VAB next to UTIL to return.

switchology.text: [P/CPG] Press the FCR FAB to access the Fire Control Radar menu.

switchology: [P/CPG] Set Sight Selector Switch to LEFT (FCR).
[P/CPG] Set FCR Mode Selector to FWD (GTM).
[P/CPG] Optionally enable TSD ATK mode and/or C-SCP to display FCR symbology on the display/HMD.
[P/CPG] From the FCR UTIL page, select the desired Priority Scheme and Scan Field-of-View.

switchology.text: [CPG] Press A/S (Arm/Safe) Pushbutton to set Master Arm ON (ARM).

switchology: [CPG] Press TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS RIGHT to select Missiles.
[CPG] Flip TEDAC Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger Switch Guard UP (Safety OFF/OPEN).
[CPG] Confirm the selected sight is the FCR.
[CPG] The FCR automatically locates and ranges the NTS (Next-to-Shoot) target.
[CPG] Verify no weapon inhibit messages are displayed in the High Action Display.
[CPG] Fire by squeezing the Left Hand Grip Weapons Trigger, second detent.
[CPG] Missile is fire-and-forget - it homes on the target autonomously after launch.

ordnance_jettison.name: Selective Stores Jettison
ordnance_jettison.notes: Chuck's Guide section 5.1 - jettison specific stations only.
steps: Press the desired Station Jettison Arm/Select Pushbutton (L OUTBD / L INBD / R INBD / R OUTBD) for the station(s) you want to jettison.
Press the JETT (Jettison) Button to jettison all selected/armed stations.

ordnance_jettison.name: Emergency Stores Jettison
ordnance_jettison.notes: Chuck's Guide section 5.2 - jettisons ALL stores at once, for emergencies.
steps: Flip the Emergency Jettison Switch Cover Guard.

systems_notes.topic: Armament overview (M139 gun, M261 rockets, Hellfire)
systems_notes.notes: The AH-64D has three primary weapons: the M139 Area Weapon System (a hydraulically steered M230 30 mm chain gun), the M261 Aerial Rocket Sub-System (19-tube launchers firing Hydra 70 / 2.75-inch rockets), and the Longbow Hellfire Modular Missile System (M299 four-rail launcher, which fires every Hellfire variant). Gun ammo is M789 HEDP (combat) or M788 TP (training), chosen in the Mission Editor; the magazine holds 1,200 rounds (300 if the Internal Auxiliary Fuel System 'Robbie tank' is installed) and fires up to about 625 rounds per minute. Rocket launchers ride all four pylons for up to 76 rockets, and each launcher is 'zoned' so a pair can carry up to three rocket types, or up to five with two pairs. Missiles: the AGM-114K is a semi-active laser missile guided by the CPG's TADS laser (or another designator); the AGM-114L is a fire-and-forget active-radar missile guided by the AN/APG-78 Fire Control Radar. Both carry a tandem-charge HEAT warhead to defeat reactive armor. The air-to-air (WAS AFT) position has no function in this DCS variant.

Types available: M151 HE ('10-pounder' high explosive for lightly armored and soft targets, point-detonating or programmable-delay fuze); M156 white phosphorus (target marking); M229 HE ('17-pounder' aerial artillery, point-detonating or programmable-delay fuze); M257 illumination; M259 white phosphorus (smokescreen concealment); M261 MPSM (multipurpose submunition, airburst just before the target, for lightly to medium armored vehicles and soft targets); M264 red phosphorus (smokescreen); M274 TP-SM 'blue spear' (training rocket with a brief smoke signature); M282 MPP (multipurpose penetrator for lightly armored vehicles and bunkers, fixed-delay fuze). On the WPN page the loaded types show as labels such as 6PD (Mk 66 motor, point-detonation fuzing, high explosive), 6RC (penetration, high explosive), 6MP (time-delay multipurpose submunition), 6IL (time-delay illumination), 6SK (time-delay smoke) and 6FL (time-delay flechette).

The pilot's main job is flying toward the target, managing countermeasure programs and flying attack profiles; the CPG powers up and runs the sensors (especially the TADS), designates and stores targets, and runs guided weapons like the Hellfire. Master Arm (the A/S button) is available in both cockpits, so either crew member can launch weapons - but TADS target designation is ultimately the CPG's job. If the pilot is incapacitated, the CPG can fly the helicopter and employ unguided weapons. Both seats configure weapons on the WPN MPD page and enter values on the KU (Keyboard Unit). The GND ORIDE button overrides the on-ground weapon safety so the crew can WAS and arm weapons on the ground. Clear communication between the two crew members is what makes the aircraft work.

systems_notes.topic: Weapon Action Switch (WAS) and trigger guard
systems_notes.notes: Selecting a weapon is called 'WASing' it (say 'wahz'). WAS FWD = G (gun), LEFT = R (rockets), RIGHT = M (Hellfire missiles), AFT = A (air-to-air, no function in this DCS variant); the WPN page changes to match. The pilot's and CPG's cyclic WAS switches override each other, and the CPG also has a WAS on the TEDAC Left Hand Grip. Important: if the CPG uses the TEDAC Left Hand Grip WAS, only the CPG's TEDAC trigger is active; if the CPG uses the cyclic WAS, only the CPG's cyclic trigger is active. The Weapons Trigger Switch has two detents (the second fires, default Spacebar) and a trigger guard that must be flipped up first - the guide recommends binding 'Weapons Trigger Guard - OPEN/CLOSE' to something easy like LSHIFT+SPACEBAR. The 'Weapons Trigger Guard Enable' special option turns the guard requirement off.

systems_notes.topic: Weapon delivery techniques (hover, running, diving fire)
systems_notes.notes: Hover Fire: flown below effective translational lift (roughly 16-24 knots), either moving or stationary. Running Fire: flown above ETL - forward airspeed adds stability and improves accuracy of unguided weapons, especially rockets. Diving Fire: an attack in a dive, typically -10 to -30 degrees of pitch; a steeper dive gives a smaller 'beaten zone' and better accuracy but needs more altitude to recover, and it can be flown from low altitude with a climb or 'bump' from behind cover, or from level flight at high altitude. Airspeed and altitude depend on the expected threat and the effect you want.

systems_notes.topic: M230 gun - ranging, turret limits and limit messages
systems_notes.notes: The gun turret can be slaved to the TADS line of sight, the IHADSS (helmet) line of sight, or fixed forward. Turret travel is +11 to -60 degrees in elevation and +/-86 degrees in azimuth. Limit messages: BAL LIMIT (sight aimed beyond the gun's maximum ballistic range), COINCIDENCE (the sight and the barrel aren't converged yet - usually while the turret is still slewing), EL LIMIT (aimed too high or too low) and AZ LIMIT (aimed beyond the azimuth limits). Ranging is either manual (a fixed range set with the MAN RNG VAB and the KU - the guide uses 800 m) or automatic (enter 'A'; the radar altimeter must be on). With the HMD as the sight and the gun WASed, the range source automatically reverts to manual so a stale range (e.g. a NAV range) can't skew the solution - you can still switch to another source afterward. Maximum supported software ballistic range is 4200 m; the guide's author likes 500-1800 m. The gun is an area-suppression weapon for soft targets, not a precision one.

systems_notes.topic: Rocket aiming - Rocket Steering Cursor, ADL and pylon articulation
systems_notes.notes: The M261 launchers hang on articulated hardpoints that move between +4 and -15 degrees in elevation (never in azimuth) so the salvo lands on your aimpoint; a PYLON LIMIT message means you've exceeded that range. The Armament Datum Line (ADL) is drawn straight out from the nose at -4.9 degrees and shown by the Head Tracker symbol - in a stable, windless hover it's level with the horizon, roughly midway in the pylons' travel. The Rocket Steering Cursor tells you which way to turn (cyclic or pedals) and what pitch you need to keep the ballistic solution inside the pylon range: it's offset right/left when the aimpoint is right/left of the ADL, lined up with the aimpoint when you're on solution, and dashed when the aimpoint is out of pylon range. The aimpoint is the helmet line-of-sight reticle when the HMD is the sight (or the TADS line of sight when it's the acquisition source). Four engagement methods: Hover Fire with HMD, Running/Diving Fire with HMD, Direct Fire with COOP Mode and TADS (clear line of sight), and Indirect Fire with COOP Mode and TADS (no line of sight needed - slave the TADS to a waypoint or target point). COOP = both crew select rockets; the CPG designates and the pilot steers and fires.

When you WAS the Hellfire, the Missile Constraints Box on the HDU monocle and TDU shows where the missile seeker is looking relative to the missile datum line (4 degrees above the horizon) - it does not map to a spot out the window. A small box (LOAL) means the seeker isn't detecting laser energy matching its assigned code (lock-on after launch); a big box (LOBL) means it's tracking a matching laser (lock-on before launch). Dashed = outside constraints or not ready; solid = inside constraints and ready to fire. The LOAL box allows a maximum launch offset of 7.5 degrees from the datum line; the LOBL box allows 20 degrees, and reverts to the LOAL box if the seeker loses the laser. With SAL missiles selected, every pylon carrying them is commanded to +4 degrees above the horizon regardless of attitude; if a pylon can't get within 10 degrees of that, a PYLON LIMIT message appears - roughly aircraft pitch of -10 to +29 degrees. You can still fire with the trigger, but a hit isn't guaranteed if the pylons can't articulate properly.

systems_notes.topic: Hellfire - missile settings, channels and laser codes
systems_notes.notes: WPN page missile settings: Type SAL (semi-active laser, AGM-114K) or RF (radio frequency, AGM-114L). For SAL, SAL 1 fires Hellfire I missiles (PRF codes only), SAL 2 fires Hellfire II (PRF and PIM codes) and AUTO picks automatically (a PIM code forces Hellfire II). Mode: NORM (all missiles guided on the priority channel), RIPL (ripple - guidance alternates between the priority and alternate channel on each launch) or MAN (manual - one missile at a time on the priority channel; the Missile Advance button on the collective/TEDAC readies the next one and does nothing outside MAN). Trajectory: DIR (direct), LO (low loft) or HI (high loft). Each SAL Hellfire has four channels, each assigned a laser code preset (a letter preset such as A, B, C or D, each editable - e.g. preset A might hold code 1688); one channel is set as PRIORITY (PRI) and one as ALTERNATE (ALT, only after a priority is chosen). Having several channels lets you retask missiles quickly when multiple designators are working together. The LST (Laser Spot Tracker) code is for the TADS laser detector, letting it slave to a JTAC's or another aircraft's laser; the LRFD code is for your own designator. The LRFD FIRST/LAST setting picks which part of the return pulse sets range (lasing through foliage: FIRST = the foliage, LAST = what's behind it). Missile icons: LS standby with no code, AR/BR... ready and scanning for that code, AT/BT... tracking that code (for RF missiles S = standby/unaligned, R = ready, T = tracking).

flight_planning_notes: Cold Start Procedure follows the guide's own A-F structure: Before Start-Up, APU Start, DMS Sweep/systems setup, IHADSS Boresight, Engine Start, After Start-Up.
Nav system (Doppler) alignment takes roughly 4-5 minutes once started - plan startup timing around this if you have a tight mission start.

qa_snippets.answer: AGM-114L is fire-and-forget - no lasing needed after launch. With FCR: set sight to FCR (LEFT), FCR mode FWD/GTM, let the radar auto-locate the Next-to-Shoot target, Master Arm ON, WAS RIGHT for missiles, fire on second trigger detent. Without FCR: same arming steps but designate the target with the TADS LRFD trigger instead of the radar.

Selective: press the Station Jettison Arm/Select button for the station(s) you want, then press JETT. Emergency (all stores at once): flip the Emergency Jettison Switch Cover Guard, then press the Emergency Jettison Switch.

Arm chaff via the ASE page VAB, set CHAFF MODE to MANUAL (single press = one dispense) or PROGRAM (set burst/salvo counts on the ASE Utility sub-page first), then press the Chaff Dispense Button on the cyclic.

Power CMWS ON, set CMWS/NAV to CMWS, choose BYPASS (fully manual - flares only dispense when you press the button) or AUTO (auto-dispenses on missile threat detection, per the preset flare program), Arm/Safe to ARM, then use the Flare Dispense Button.
For a forced landing (flares are a fire hazard): CMWS Power ON, Arm/Safe to ARM, flip the Flare Jettison Cover up, then switch JETTISON up.
Power ON, set brightness as required, CMWS/NAV switch to CMWS, choose Bypass or Auto for flares, set Arm/Safe to ARM, then read launch direction and threat info off the CMWS Indicator Display.

LOBL (Lock-On Before Launch) is the primary method: power up TADS/FLIR/laser, Master Arm ON, WAS RIGHT to select Missiles, set missile type to SAL/mode NORMAL/trajectory DIR, set laser codes, select TADS sight, lase the target with the LRFD trigger, verify PRI CHAN TRK shows in the display, then fire on the left grip's second trigger detent while continuing to lase until impact.

question_hints: how do I start the apu
qa_snippets.answer: Flip the APU Start Button Guard, then press the APU Start Button for 1-2 seconds and release. Watch for APU START on the EUFD during spin-up, then APU POWER ON once complete.

question_hints: how do I fire the gun
qa_snippets.answer: Set Sight Select Switch to FWD (HMD), Master Arm ON via the A/S pushbutton, WAS UP to select the gun, flip the trigger guard up, set your range/burst limit via the VABs, then fire on the second trigger detent (default Spacebar).

Master Arm ON, WAS LEFT to select Rockets, flip the trigger guard up, select rocket type and set range/salvo via the VABs, steer the Rocket Steering Cursor onto the target, then fire on the second trigger detent.

Chuck's Guide does not include a dedicated post-flight shutdown checklist as of this extraction - it focuses on Cold Start in depth. As a placeholder, the general DCS Apache shutdown pattern is: power levers to OFF/idle-cutoff, engage rotor brake once rotor RPM has decayed, then battery/master ignition OFF - but this has NOT been verified against the guide and should be confirmed in-sim or against another source before relying on it.
